W4.evidence: It is now an error to pass more command-arguments than are expected.

W5.evidence: $ node example.js a b c; error: too many arguments. Expected 0 arguments but got 3.

H1-a.evidence: You can declare the expected arguments. The help will then be more accurate too.

Y1.evidence:
By default, if is not an error to pass excess command-arguments. This may sometimes be as intended but
will often mean a command-line error by the user will be silently ignored.
